### ⚑ Section 7 · Q.7 · 4. — 1 mark

> How are the people in the picture helping the community? \_\_\_\_\_

- **Answer: They are keeping the place clean by sweeping, planting trees and repairing the bench, so everyone can use it.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Gives two ways from the picture (cleaning/sweeping, planting, repairing), or one way with why it helps everyone.
  - partial (0.5 marks): Gives only one way, with no reason.
  - none (0 marks): No answer, or an answer that does not match the picture.
- Model answer: They are cleaning the area, planting trees and repairing the bench for everyone to use.

### ⚑ Section 8 · Q.8 · 1. — 2 marks

> Why do you think it is important to save money?

- **Answer: Saving money helps us meet our future needs and pay for emergencies such as illness. Money kept in a bank is safe.**
- Answer points:
  - For future needs (studies, buying things later) (1 mark)
  - For emergencies / sudden needs, or money is kept safe in a bank (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Two sensible reasons (future needs, emergencies, keeping money safe).
  - partial (1 mark): One sensible reason.
  - none (0 marks): No sensible reason.
- Model answer: It is important to save money so that we have money for our future needs and for emergencies. Banks keep our saved money safe.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.8 l.9-15

### ⚑ Section 8 · Q.8 · 2. — 2 marks

> What is the role of Public places?

- **Answer: Public places help people by providing services related to health, safety, cleanliness and the environment (e.g. hospitals, banks, post offices, police stations). They are also used for playing, relaxing and meeting others.**
- Answer points:
  - They provide services for everyone (health, safety, cleanliness, environment) (1 mark)
  - An example or another use (playing, relaxing, meeting others; hospital, bank, post office, police station, park) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): States that public places serve everyone / give services, with an example or second use.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one point, or only lists examples of public places.
  - none (0 marks): No sensible answer.
- Model answer: Public places help people by giving services like health, safety and cleanliness. For example, a hospital treats sick people and a park is used for playing and relaxing.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.11 l.19-23; Ch 1 (deev101), p.5 l.8-14
- Teacher note: "Public" is printed with a capital P. Kept as printed.

- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.11 l.19-23; Ch 1 (deev101), p.5 l.8-14
- Teacher note: "Public" is printed with a capital P. Kept as printed.

#### ⚑ Section 8 · Q.8 · 3. — 2 marks

> Which equipment did Mallika use to make announcements?

- **Answer: Mallika used a microphone to make announcements (at the Van Mahotsav celebration).**
- Answer points:
  - Microphone (mic / mike) (2 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Microphone (mic / mike), in a word or a sentence.
  - partial (1 mark): A near answer such as "loudspeaker", "speaker" or "sound system".
  - none (0 marks): Any other equipment, or no answer.
- Model answer: Mallika used a microphone to make announcements.
- Source: Ch 1 (deev101), p.9 l.2-4
- Teacher note: A one-word answer (microphone) for 2 marks as printed. Full marks for "microphone" / "mic" / "mike"; a full sentence is not required.

#### Section 8 · Q.8 · 4. — 2 marks

> How does the post office help people stay connected with each other?

- **Answer: The post office collects letters, parcels and important documents, sorts them by region and delivers them to people in other places, so people can keep in touch. It also helped send money (money orders).**
- Answer points:
  - Sends/delivers letters, parcels and documents (1 mark)
  - To people in other places/cities, so they keep in touch (or sorts by region / money orders) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Says the post office sends/delivers letters or parcels AND that this keeps people in different places in touch.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one of the two ideas.
  - none (0 marks): No sensible answer.
- Model answer: The post office sends our letters and parcels to people living in other cities. So we can keep in touch with our family and friends far away.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.2 l.19-24; p.3 l.14-17; p.8 l.20-22
